subject: Temporary throughput buffer & queue isolation request — BlueHarbor Q4 peak
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir@blueharbor.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@blueharbor.com>, procurement@blueharbor.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Request: temporary throughput guarantee & queue isolation for Q4 peak

Hi Avery,

Quick context: our freight planning app will run a time-limited promotion Nov 15–Dec 31 and we expect a spike in inference volume for shipment ETA predictions and reranking. We've modeled a 6x increase in token throughput during peak windows (08:00–20:00 ET).

Can Redwood provide a temporary throughput guarantee or queue isolation on our dedicated pool so we don't see latency spikes / queued requests for the promotion? Our procurement/legal team is asking for short-term SLA language and a price uplift if needed.

I've attached a forecast (BH_Q4_traffic_forecast.xlsx) — it includes hourly profiles. High level asks:
- Dedicated buffer of reserved GPUs (or guaranteed throughput) for Nov 15–Dec 31
- A queue-isolation policy so background batch jobs from other tenants don't push our tail latency above 250 ms p50/p95 targets
- A one-page amendment or addendum we can sign so procurement can approve the spend quickly

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

Samir Khan
Head of Platform Integrations
BlueHarbor Logistics
samir@blueharbor.com
+1 617-555-0198

[Attachment: BH_Q4_traffic_forecast.xlsx]

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:00:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary throughput guarantee & queue isolation for Q4 peak

Hi Samir — thanks for the note and the forecast.

We can absolutely support a temporary carveout for a bounded term; a couple quick clarifying questions before we propose language and pricing:
1) Peak windows: is the 08:00–20:00 ET window fixed every day or are there specific high-volume dates (e.g., Black Friday)?
2) Is the 6x uplift driven by more concurrent requests or longer context lengths per request?
3) Do you need absolute p95 latency guarantees (e.g., 250 ms) or is a relative uplift cap (no more than 2x baseline p95) acceptable?

I've looped in Marissa (sales lead) and Ben (capacity/ops) to draft an amendment. We'll come back with an options matrix (throughput uplift vs. reserved GPU count vs. uplifted pricing) and an SLA addendum for procurement/Legal. If useful, we can include a short preemptible fallback that reduces cost while preserving critical latency windows.

Available for a quick sync today at 2pm ET — let me know.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Director, North America
Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.com
[Redwood logo]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -08:00
Subject: INTERNAL: draft terms for BlueHarbor temporary throughput buffer (RWD-8421-BH)

Folks — internal note so we have a single source of truth before we reply to Samir. Summary of options we can offer:

Option A — Guaranteed reserved GPUs (cleanest)
- Reserve 4x current pool size (based on forecast) for 6 weeks (Nov 15–Dec 31)
- Price: 30% uplift on current committed rate for that capacity window
- SLA addendum: guarantee p95 <= 250 ms for requests routed to the reserved pool; Redwood to provide incident credits for violations (pro-rated).

Option B — Throughput guard + queue isolation (lower cost)
- Keep current reserved pool but configure a tenant-level queue buffer for 08:00–20:00 ET; assign weighted request slots so BlueHarbor gets 60% of real-time capacity during windows
- Price: 15% uplift + usage overage at standard hosted rate
- SLA: best-effort p95 target with routing priority; we include an operational playbook for unusual spikes.

Option C — Hybrid with preemptible burst cap
- 2x reserved GPUs + burstable shared capacity with guaranteed preemption window; cheaper but with fallback policy
- Price: 20% uplift; clear preemption notification/latency expectations

Operational notes: Ben recommends Option A if the forecast is accurate — avoids noisy neighbor effects and simplifies latency guarantees. Lauren: we will need a short amendment (1 page) that defines the temporary term, measurement windows, monitoring/alerting behavior, and credit calc. I'll attach a draft amendment and a short monitoring dashboard spec for the customer.

Next actions:
- Ben to confirm estimated GPU count and OSS/quantization assumptions by EOD Tue
- Lauren to review amendment & redline by Wed morning
- Avery to propose preferred option to Samir + attach draft amendment and DocuSign link

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: draft-sla-amendment-RWD-8421.pdf]

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@blueharbor.com>, procurement@blueharbor.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 14:15:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary throughput guarantee & queue isolation for Q4 peak

Hi Samir — thanks again for the forecast and the quick sync yesterday. Per our internal review we recommend Option A (reserved capacity) to meet your p95 latency target reliably for the promotion.

Summary of proposed terms (high level):
- Term: Nov 15, 2026 00:00 ET – Dec 31, 2026 23:59 ET
- Capacity: 4 additional reserved GPU units (non-shared) allocated to BlueHarbor during peak hours; config mirrors your production model profile
- Monitoring: Ping/trace-based latency SLOs at p50/p95; access to a dedicated dashboard and daily ingestion of tail-latency reports
- SLA: p95 <= 250 ms for requests routed to reserved pool. If we miss p95 more than 2 times in a 7-day window, customer will receive a pro-rated credit (calculation in attached addendum).
- Pricing: 30% uplift on committed monthly capacity for duration; one-time operational onboarding fee (waived for this deal)

We have attached a short amendment (draft-sla-amendment-RWD-8421.pdf) and a DocuSign link to execute once you confirm the option. If procurement wants the hybrid or guard option instead, we can surface Option B/C pricing quickly.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/RWD-8421-BH/sla-amendment
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/8421

If that looks good, we can get the amendment signed this week and schedule an ops onboarding with Ben to validate model runtime settings and KV cache warmup before Nov 15.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Director, North America
Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.com
[Attachment: draft-sla-amendment-RWD-8421.pdf]
